info.title: True Fit Partner API
info.description:
These APIs can be used to manage True Fit profiles on behalf of your own users and to
request size recommendations for retailer products.

# Getting Started

Here are the general concepts - please see further below for the specific endpoint
documentation.

## Base URL

Every path in this reference is relative to the base URL, which already includes the
`/api` prefix:

```
https://partner.truefitcorp.com/api
```

## Authentication

All `/partner/{partnerId}/**` endpoints use HTTP Basic authentication. The **username is
empty** and the **password is your partner API key**:

```
Authorization: Basic <base64(":" + apiKey)>
```

Note the leading colon. `base64(apiKey)` without it has no separator and is rejected
with `401`.

An unknown or disabled `partnerId` returns `404` **before** credentials are checked, so a
`404` on your first call points at the `partnerId` or the environment, not at the key.

`GET /id-sync` is authenticated differently - it is signed with HMAC-SHA256 rather than
Basic auth. See that endpoint for the signing scheme.

## Identifying a user

Partner endpoints operate on a True Fit user, not on your identifier directly.
`GET /id-sync` creates that user and maps one of your identifiers to it. Call it once per
user, store the `tfPartnerUserId` it returns, and drive every later request from that.

Except for `POST /general-guidance/bulk`, every endpoint needs a user identifier as a
query parameter:

* `tfPartnerUserId` - the identifier returned by `GET /id-sync`. Preferred: it is a
  durable handle on one specific True Fit user and its data.
* `partnerUserId` - your own identifier for the user, as passed to `GET /id-sync`.

Supply at least one; omitting both returns `400`. If you send both, `tfPartnerUserId`
takes precedence. An identifier that was never synced returns `401 Unknown partner user`,
which means "call `GET /id-sync` first" rather than "bad credentials".

## Profiles

A profile is the entity that holds information about the person being shopped for -
department, alias, measurements, and closet items. When a profile is created it is
assigned a `profileId`, which is then used in the path of the measurements, closet, and
recommendation endpoints.

A user may have several profiles, one per person they shop for. List them with
`GET /profile` and address them explicitly by `profileId`; there is no implicit "current"
profile in this API.

Profiles you create record your `partnerId` as their `originStore`.

## Getting a size recommendation

A profile needs measurements, closet items, or both before it can be sized: a profile
carrying neither has nothing to size against and returns `incompleteProfile`. Add
measurements with `PUT /profile/{profileId}/measurements` and closet items with
`POST /profile/{profileId}/closet`, then call
`POST /profile/{profileId}/recommendation/bulk`.

Profile writes trigger asynchronous body estimation, so a recommendation requested
immediately after one may return `userEstimationInProgress`. Retry after a short delay.

When no profile exists - anonymous visitors, or a product page before registration -
use `POST /general-guidance/bulk` instead. It returns how a product ran for shoppers
generally, needs no user identifier, and is the natural fallback when a recommendation
returns `incompleteProfile` or `noProfile`.

## Example Flow - Product Page

1. Once per user, call `GET /id-sync` and persist the returned `tfPartnerUserId`.
2. Call `GET /profile` to list the user's profiles.
3. If the list is empty, give the user an opportunity to register, then create a profile
   with `POST /profile`.
4. Add what you know about the user: `PUT /profile/{profileId}/measurements`, and
   `POST /profile/{profileId}/closet` for garments they already own.
5. Call `POST /profile/{profileId}/recommendation/bulk` with the products on the page and
   present `recommendedSize` for each successful result.
6. For products that return `success: false`, or when no profile exists, fall back to
   `POST /general-guidance/bulk`.

## Bulk requests

Both bulk endpoints take a JSON **array** of 1 to 100 items and return an array of the
**same length and in the same order**, so results can be matched to requests by position.
Each result also echoes the `retailerDomain`, `productId`, and `locale` you sent.

Failures are per item: each result carries `success: true` with its data, or
`success: false` with an `error` string. One unrecognised product does not fail the batch,
and the HTTP status is still a success status.

`retailerDomain` accepts a hostname or a full URL, from which only the hostname is used -
protocol, port, path, and query string are discarded, and matching is case-insensitive.
`www.` is not stripped, so confirm with True Fit which exact hostnames are registered for
your retailers.

## Request bodies

Enum values are documented in their canonical lowercase form but matched
case-insensitively, so `Womens` and `womens` are equally valid - the stored and returned
value is always lowercase. Fields not listed in a schema are ignored rather than rejected.

## General API Behavior

* Success statuses vary by endpoint. Empty-bodied writes return `200` in some places and
  `204` in others, and both bulk endpoints return `201`. Treat any 2xx as success rather
  than matching an exact code.
* A `400 - Bad Request` is returned when a body or query string fails validation, or when
  no user identifier is supplied.
* A `401 - Unauthorized` is returned for a missing or wrong API key, and for a user
  identifier that has no True Fit mapping.
* A `404 - Not Found` is returned for an unknown or disabled `partnerId`, and for a
  `profileId` that does not exist or does not belong to the identified user. Another
  user's profile returns `404` rather than `403` so that the API cannot be used to detect
  whether a profile exists.
* It is possible for any endpoint to return a `500 - Internal Server Error` if an
  unexpected error is encountered.
* Validation failures carry a field-keyed error map and, unlike other errors, no
  `statusCode` field:

```json
{ "message": "Validation failed", "error": { "0.retailerDomain": "Invalid input: expected string, received undefined" } }
```

Array indices appear as the first path segment, so `0.retailerDomain` is the
`retailerDomain` field of the first item in a bulk request. All other errors use the
standard shape:

```json
{ "statusCode": 404, "message": "Profile not found", "error": "Not Found" }
```

## Rate limits

No rate limits are enforced today. Expected request volume should be agreed during
onboarding.

get.summary: Create a True Fit user for one of your users
get.description:
Creates a True Fit user and maps one of your user identifiers to it. Call this once per
user, before any other endpoint.

**Sync each user exactly once and store the returned `tfPartnerUserId`.** Re-syncing a
`partnerUserId` that has already been synced is not supported: it issues a new
`tfPartnerUserId` and detaches the profiles, measurements, and closet items written
under the previous one.

### Signing the request

Requests are signed with HMAC-SHA256 using the shared partner secret issued during
onboarding. Build the canonical string from every query parameter **except** `hash`,
sorted by parameter name, URL-encoding each value:

```
canonical = "partnerId=<value>&partnerUserId=<value>"          # sorted, hash excluded
hash      = hex(hmac_sha256(partnerSecret, canonical))
```

`redirectUri`, when present, participates in the signature like any other parameter.
The comparison is timing-safe and the hash must be lowercase hex.

This endpoint does **not** use Basic authentication - do not send an `Authorization`
header.

parameters.name: partnerId
parameters.description: Your partner identifier, issued during onboarding.

parameters.name: partnerUserId
parameters.description: Your own stable identifier for the user.

parameters.name: redirectUri
parameters.description:
When supplied, the response is a `302` redirect to this URI instead of a JSON body.
Intended for browser-based flows; server-to-server integrations should omit it.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: Lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 signature over the other query parameters.

tfPartnerUserId.description:
True Fit's identifier for this partner user. Prefixed with `p-`. Store it
and send it as the `tfPartnerUserId` query parameter on later requests.

302.description: Returned instead of `200` when `redirectUri` was supplied.

401.description: The `hash` parameter is missing or the signature does not match.

get.description:
Returns every profile belonging to the user, oldest first is not guaranteed - treat the
order as unspecified and address profiles by `profileId`. A user with no profiles yet
returns an empty array.

post.description:
Creates a profile for the user. The created profile records your `partnerId` as its
`originStore`. An empty object is a valid body; both fields are optional.

put.description:
Partially updates the profile. Only the fields you send are changed. Updating a profile
re-runs body estimation, so a subsequent recommendation may briefly return
`userEstimationInProgress`.

200.description:
The profile's measurements. Each exact measurement is echoed as submitted and
additionally carries a normalized value in True Fit's standard unit (inches for
lengths and girths, pounds for weight, months for age).

put.description:
Upserts the measurements you send. Measurement points you omit are left untouched;
this is not a full replacement of the measurement set.

Writing measurements re-runs body estimation, so a recommendation requested
immediately afterwards may return `userEstimationInProgress`. Retry after a short delay.

200.description:
The profile's closet items. String fields are returned lowercased - `sellingSize`
is the exception and is stored and returned verbatim.

post.description:
Adds a garment the user owns. The submitted combination of `brand`, `department`,
`category`, `sellingLocale`, `hierarchyLabels`, `sellingSize`, and
`sizeVariants.sizeType` must resolve to a size that exists in True Fit's catalogue -
arbitrary garments cannot be added. See the integration guide for how to pick values
that validate.

Adding a closet item re-runs body estimation, so a recommendation requested
immediately afterwards may return `userEstimationInProgress`.

201.description: Closet item added. No response body.

put.description:
Partially updates a closet item. The fields you send are merged over the stored item and
the merged result is re-validated against True Fit's size catalogue, so a partial update
can be rejected because of fields you did not send.

200.description: Closet item updated. No response body.

post.summary: Recommend sizes for up to 100 products
post.description:
Returns a recommended size per product for the given profile.

The response array has the **same length and order as the request array**, so results
can be matched positionally. Each result also echoes the `retailerDomain`, `productId`,
and `locale` you sent. Failures are per item: a product that cannot be recommended
returns `success: false` with an `error`, and does not fail the other items.

This is a `POST` because the product list is sent in the body; it has no side effects
and returns `201`.

201.description: One result per requested item, in request order.

post.summary: Get aggregate fit guidance for up to 100 products
post.description:
Returns crowd-sourced fit guidance for products - how the product ran for other
shoppers - without reference to any individual user.

Unlike every other endpoint, this one needs **no user identifier**: the partner API key
alone authorizes it, and no `partnerUserId` or `tfPartnerUserId` query parameter is
required. Use it for anonymous visitors and for product pages where no profile exists.

The response array has the same length and order as the request array, and failures are
per item.

201.description: One result per requested item, in request order.

value.recommendationMessage: Most shoppers found this ran small - consider sizing up.

partnerApiKey.description:
Empty username, partner API key as the password:
`Authorization: Basic <base64(":" + apiKey)>`.

partnerId.name: partnerId
partnerId.description: Your partner identifier, issued during onboarding.

profileId.name: profileId
profileId.description:
A profile belonging to the identified user, from `GET /profile`. Profiles belonging to
another user return `404` rather than `403`, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe
for the existence of other users' profiles.

closetItemId.name: closetItemId
closetItemId.description: A closet item identifier, from the `closetId` field of `GET /closet`.

partnerUserId.name: partnerUserId
partnerUserId.description:
Your own identifier for the user, as passed to `GET /id-sync`. Send either this or
`tfPartnerUserId`; omitting both returns `400`. If both are sent, `tfPartnerUserId` wins.

tfPartnerUserId.name: tfPartnerUserId
tfPartnerUserId.description:
True Fit's identifier for the user, returned by `GET /id-sync`. Send either this or
`partnerUserId`; omitting both returns `400`. Takes precedence when both are sent.

Unauthorized.description:
Missing or invalid Basic credentials, or a user identifier that does not match a known
partner user.

unknownUser.summary: The identifier has no True Fit mapping - call GET /id-sync first

UnsupportedPartner.description:
The `partnerId` is unknown or disabled. Returned before credentials are checked, so an
invalid API key against an unknown partner is a `404`, not a `401`.

ProfileNotFound.description:
The `profileId` does not exist or does not belong to the identified user. Also returned
when the `partnerId` is unknown or disabled.

ValidationFailed.description:
The request body or query string failed schema validation. `error` maps each failing
field path to its message; array indices appear as the first path segment.

error.0.retailerDomain: Invalid input: expected string, received undefined

value.message: tfPartnerUserId or partnerUserId query parameter is required

UnvalidatedClosetSize.description:
A server error. On these endpoints it also indicates a closet item that does not match a
size in True Fit's catalogue, in which case retrying the identical payload will not
succeed. Verify the `brand`, `department`, `category`, `sellingLocale`, `hierarchyLabels`,
`sellingSize`, and `sizeVariants.sizeType` combination; `sellingSize: null` is not
accepted.

ValidationError.description: Schema validation failure. Note this body carries no `statusCode`.

error.description: Failing field path to error message.

Department.description:
Garment department. Matched case-insensitively - `Womens` and `womens` are both accepted
- and stored lowercased.

ClosetCategory.description: Garment category. Matched case-insensitively and stored lowercased.

SizeType.description: Size range the garment belongs to. Matched case-insensitively and stored lowercased.

MeasurementPoint.description: A point on the body that can carry a measurement. Case-sensitive.

GeneralMeasurementValue.description: A qualitative measurement - how the user describes a body point or fit preference.

ExactMeasurementValue.description:
A numeric measurement. Compound values use both unit pairs: 5'6" is
`{ unit: "ft", value: 5, secondUnit: "in", secondValue: 6 }`.

unit.description: Primary unit - `ft` for feet, `kg` for kilograms, and so on.

secondUnit.description: Secondary unit, used alongside the primary - `in` for inches with `ft` for feet.

normalizedValue.description: The measurement converted to True Fit's standard unit for that point.

normalizedUnit.description:
Standard unit for the point - `in` for lengths and girths, `lb` for weight,
`month` for age.

MeasurementsRequest.description:
Measurements to upsert. Points you omit are left unchanged. At least one of the two
maps should be present; an empty object is accepted and is a no-op.

exactMeasurements.description: Numeric measurements keyed by measurement point.

generalMeasurements.description:
Qualitative measurements keyed by measurement point - how the user describes a body
point, or how they prefer a garment to fit there.

department.description: The department the user primarily shops.

alias.description: A label for the profile, shown to the user. Not required to be unique.

UpdateProfileRequest.description: Every field is optional; only the fields you send are changed.

registeredAt.description: When the user registered with you. Set once when the user creates an account.

savedAt.description: When the user last explicitly saved the profile.

userId.description: True Fit's internal user identifier. Not required for any partner call.

isActive.description:
Whether this is the active profile in a browser session. Always `false` for partner
requests, which carry no browser session - ignore it.

estimatedDob.description: Date of birth inferred from the profile's age measurement, when available.

originStore.description:
Where the profile was created. Profiles you create through this API carry your
`partnerId`.

CreateClosetItemRequest.description:
A garment the user owns. The combination of fields must resolve to a size in True Fit's
catalogue or the request is rejected - see the integration guide.

hierarchyLabels.description:
The garment's position in the brand's category hierarchy, coarsest first. Must match
the hierarchy True Fit holds for that brand, department, and category. Stored
lowercased.

sellingLocale.description: Two-letter country code for the market the garment was bought in. Stored lowercased.

sellingSize.description:
The size on the garment's label, exactly as printed. Stored and returned verbatim,
not lowercased. Always send a real size - `null` is not accepted.

fitAttributes.description: Free-form fit notes about this garment as string key/value pairs. Defaults to `null`.

UpdateClosetItemRequest.description:
Every field is optional. The fields you send are merged over the stored item and the
merged result is re-validated against True Fit's catalogue.

closetId.description: Identifier for this closet item, used in the item's path.

retailerDomain.description:
The retailer the product belongs to, as a hostname. A full URL is also accepted -
only the hostname is used, and protocol, port, path, and query string are discarded.
`www.` is **not** stripped, so the hostname must match the mapping True Fit holds for
that retailer. Matching is case-insensitive. Ask True Fit to register any retailer
domain you intend to send.

locale.description:
Locale for the product data and any returned copy, as `language_COUNTRY`. Defaults
to the retailer's primary locale when omitted.

BulkRequest.description: Between 1 and 100 items. Duplicate products are permitted and each gets its own result.

BulkRecommendationResult.description: One result, echoing the request item's fields. Match results to requests by position.

recommendedSize.description: The recommended size label, as the retailer prints it.

error.description:
Why no size was returned.

Domain resolution:
  * `Invalid retailerDomain` - the value could not be parsed as a hostname.
  * `Unsupported retailer domain` - the hostname is not mapped to a retailer.
  * `No recommendation returned for product` - the product is unknown to True Fit.

Fit outcomes:
  * `incompleteProfile` - the profile lacks the measurements needed for this garment.
  * `noProfile` - the profile no longer exists.
  * `userEstimationInProgress` - body estimation is still running after a
    profile, measurement, or closet write. Retry after a short delay.
  * `noSizesFitTheUser` - no stocked size fits.
  * `invalidGender` - the product's department does not apply to this profile.
  * `unrecommendableDepartment` - the product is in a department True Fit does
    not size, such as accessories.
  * `productMissingData` - the product lacks the garment data needed to size it.
  * `recommendationDisabled` - recommendations are turned off for that retailer.
  * `error` - an unexpected failure. Safe to retry.

BulkGeneralGuidanceResult.description: One result, echoing the request item's fields. Match results to requests by position.

recommendationSummary.description: Short headline describing how the product runs, localized to `locale`.

recommendationMessage.description: Longer explanation suitable for display, localized to `locale`.
recommendationMessage.example: Most shoppers found this ran small - consider sizing up.

error.description:
Why no guidance was returned.
  * `Invalid retailerDomain` - the value could not be parsed as a hostname.
  * `Unsupported retailer domain` - the hostname is not mapped to a retailer.
  * `No general guidance returned for product` - the product is unknown, or
    too few shoppers have rated it to produce guidance.
examples: No general guidance returned for product
